newsitem.title: USA: World microprocessor sales seen up 32 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: World microprocessor sales seen up 32 pct in 1997.

text.p: Worldwide revenues from microprocessor integrated circuits should grow 32 percent in 1997 to $22.5 billion, according to a research report issued on Tuesday.
The report, issued jointly by Forward Concepts and Micrologic Research, said 1996 worldwide integrated circuit shipments should reach $17.1 billion, compared with $14.3 billion in 1995.

Forward Concepts is a 12-year-old firm that has focused on markets for computerized digital signal-processor products. Tempe, Arizona-based Micrologic Research has published the IC revenue forecast for four years, a spokesman said.

The study also says the microcontroller market will reach $11.5 billion by the end of 1996, up seven percent from $10.7 billion in sales the previous year. Shipments in 1997 are expected to grow 28 percent to $14.7 billion.
Digital signal-processor chip sales should rise about 39 percent in 1996 to $2.4 billion, while 1997 sales are expected to jump 52 percent to $3.6 billion.

The 550-page study forecasts that microprocessor shipments will grow to over $49 billion by 2001, microcontroller shipments will exceed $39 billion and digital signal processor chips will pass the $12 billion mark.
